candidate.paraphrase: Treat surrogate Hessian decay as a cautious wrapper around first-order steps for expectation-constrained objectives, and ask whether that transfer helps batched chance constraints on trimmed-mean objectives under heavy-tailed stochastic gradients without pretending the wrapper creates new theory.

closest_neighbor.paraphrase: The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.
